issue_context.title: Arrow function class fields transform `this` to `undefined`
comments:
**Out of the topic of this issue** but my recommendation is to not use anonymous functions when the function is named. Arrow functions are meant to be passed to other functions when they are unnamed. When you assign an anonymous function to a named variable, you have already named it, so this is not considered a good idea.

Also, from the performance perspective, doing this may prevent the browser engine to inline the calls to these lambdas because the arrow functions are usually calculated **during runtime**. 

<details>
<summary>Benchmarks</summary>

About 50% slower than a free function and 10% slower than a method function. You may not notice it in a simple function that calls `this.setState` which probably will not be inlined anyway, but when inlining is important it can have a huge effect. 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16418197/103407457-5b717480-4b24-11eb-9317-c33c76a6df8b.png)
https://jsbench.me/g4kjcq9j3s/1

cc: @rinick @maxjoehnk @mischnic 

</details>

Interesting. I'm actually only using this kind of function when I'm passing it out of the current scope. E.g. in my example this method is part of a context object which is used in other components and I prefer this syntax to the bind calls in the constructor.
But maybe one could write a transform which transforms arrow functions to method functions with `bind(this)`.

> Interesting. I'm actually only using this kind of function when I'm passing it out of the current scope. E.g. in my example, this method is part of a context object which is used in other components and I prefer this syntax to the bind calls in the constructor.

If you bind it in a constructor, then there is nothing holding you back from converting it to a class method (I don't have a full context). This function seems simple enough to not have much performance difference. 

Firefox docs have a good explanation of some of the performance issues of passing lambdas directly to `addEventListener` instead of binding.

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/EventTarget/addEventListener#Memory_issues


> But maybe one could write a transform which transforms arrow functions to method functions with bind(this).

There is a babel plugin for that 😉: https://babeljs.io/docs/en/babel-plugin-transform-arrow-functions

```
 ["@babel/plugin-transform-arrow-functions", { "spec": true }]
```

Another note: The browser engine writers may see that lambdas are so much used instead of function (in a theoretically wrong context), that they may add an optimization to work around it.
